subject: Post-discovery: model-fit proposals + multilingual QA plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@globextech.com>
Cc: Anil Suresh <anil.suresh@globextech.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & suggested next steps from today's discovery

Hi Lydia / Anil,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about the product search and support routing use-cases at GlobexTech. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Key goals you reiterated: EU language parity for search results, and improved brevity/accuracy in APAC automated replies (focus: JA/KO/VI/TH/ID).
- Performance constraints: sub-150ms p99 for short search completions in EU region; tolerance for higher latency on batch offline reranks.
- Safety/compliance: you need audit logs and regional data residency in EU for PII-containing prompts.

Proposed immediate actions (we can do these in parallel):
1) Model-fit evaluation: we'll run a two-week evaluation comparing Redwood-Large-v2-8k (fp16) and the 13B quantized candidate (open-13b-8bit) across your prompt set. We think Redwood-Large gives better latency/quality for EN/FR/DE, while the 13B quantized may be better for some APAC languages after targeted fine-tuning.
2) Prompt set collection: thank you for sharing the initial sample during the call. Please upload the full prompt set (incl. negative examples and label mappings) to the Drive folder below. Format we prefer: CSV with columns: id, locale, prompt, expected_output, category.
3) Locale QA plan: we'll run locale-specific token-level and semantic-similarity benchmarks (chrF + BLEURT) and a human-pass/fail check for edge cases in Polish and Hungarian plus JA/KO/VI.
4) Compliance: we'll provision a dedicated EU evaluation queue on Redwood Dedicated so data stays in-region and audit logs are captured.

Deliverables we will share by next Wednesday (10/27):
- Run-level report with latency/quality tradeoffs per locale (PDF)
- Shared prompt harness + short README (Drive link)
- Pilot plan with canary rollout recommendations and early rollback criteria

I attached a short template for the prompt CSV and the evaluation plan (eu-apac-eval-plan.xlsx). Let me know if the timeline works and I will schedule a 30m sync with Neha and our ML lead, Marissa, to walk through the eval config.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: globex-prod-promptset.csv (template), eu-apac-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation plan)
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@globextech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Anil Suresh <anil.suresh@globextech.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up & suggested next steps from today's discovery

Thanks Marcus — this is super helpful. A few clarifications: 

- We can commit to providing ~3k labelled prompts across EU (EN/FR/DE/PL/HU) and APAC (JA/KO/VI/TH/ID). We'll de-identify PII before upload.
- Regarding latency SLAs: the 150ms p99 is for the edge retrieval + prompt passthrough. I know that will affect model choice; happy to accept slightly higher p99 for APAC languages if quality is materially better.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 evidence and confirmation that Dedicated evaluation queues will not export data outside EU.

Next: we'll upload prompt CSV and a short scoring rubric by Friday 10/23. Can we do the sync on Monday 10/26 at 10:00 AM UTC? Neha and Marissa from your side were fine in the call — please invite them.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Search Product
GlobexTech
lydia.park@globextech.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: plan for GlobexTech eval + immediate asks

Team — quick internal note ahead of Monday's sync with Globex: 

On model selection:
- Start with Redwood-Large-v2-8k (fp16) and Open-13B-8bit quantized (candidate). Configs: 8k context for search concision tests; 16k only for long-form support reply tests. Include fallback to Redwood-Medium-4k for latency-critical endpoints.
- For APAC, we should include tokenizers and vocab sanity checks for JA/KO/VI/TH/ID; early signs from previous runs show Vietnamese and Thai require adjusted byte-pair merges.

On evaluations:
- Autometrics: chrF, BLEURT, and a custom 'answer-precision' metric (binary) based on their rubric.
- Human-in-the-loop: 200 cases per locale (stratified by category) for pass/fail. We'll use the in-house QA pool and tag with locale and severity.

Compliance/infra:
- Sergio, please confirm we can provision a dedicated EU evaluation queue (data-residency + audit logging) by 10/26. If there are gating tickets, flag them.
- Rishi, can you prepare a short SOC2 evidence pack and PII handling summary for Globex? They asked specifically for evidence of logs retention and KMS usage.

Attachments to prep before Monday: globex-prod-promptset.csv (sample populated) and a link to the eval harness. Marcus will send invites.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@globextech.com>, Anil Suresh <anil.suresh@globextech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + calendar invite: model-fit + multilingual QA sync (Mon 10/26 10:00 UTC)

Hi Lydia / Anil — thanks for confirming the upload timeline. We received the first batch and I can confirm the folder looks good. Per their ask, attaching the items we discussed: the populated prompt CSV (globex-prod-promptset.csv) and the evaluation plan spreadsheet.

Quick summary of what we'll cover in tomorrow's 30m sync (agenda):
- Walk through the prompt CSV format and mapping to evaluation categories (5m)
- Review the two candidate model families, with expected latency/quality tradeoffs by locale (10m)
- Demo the in-house eval harness and how we'll report results (7m)
- Next steps and acceptance criteria for pilot: sign-off criteria + canary rollout plan (8m)

Notes on quality regressions / risks to call out before the run:
- Polish/Hungarian: inflection and morphological variation cause false negatives in simple string-match QA. We'll prioritize semantic metrics and increase human sample counts for these locales.
- Vietnamese/Thai: tokenization edge-cases have previously led to hallucination in short-context prompts; add aggressive pre-tokenization checks and normalization in the harness.
- Japanese/Korean: ensure base tokenizers and encoding flags are set to avoid full-width/half-width mismatch causing scoring noise.

Action items (owner / due):
- Globex: upload full labeled prompt set (Marcus noted receiving initial batch) — due 10/23 (Lydia)
- Redwood infra: provision EU eval queue + audit logs (Sergio) — due 10/26
- Redwood security: SOC2 evidence pack + PII handling doc (Rishi) — due 10/26
- Redwood ML: initial run configs + metric dashboard (Marissa) — due 10/30

Links & artifacts:
- Prompt folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-harness
- Eval dashboard (preview): https://redwood-internal.example/eval-dashboard?run=GLX-4821
- Deal in CRM: https://hubspot.example/deal/GLX-4821

I'll send the calendar invite for Mon 10/26 10:00 UTC (30m). If any of the internal owners see infeasible dates, shout here and we'll rebook.

Regards,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
